foundations.summary: Retains verified provider artifacts and imports locked OpenAPI, rendered-reference, bundle, and GraphQL sources into closed canonical operation descriptors and source-selected event/batch inventories while preserving unresolved evidence as explicit gaps. Legacy v1/v2 source_contract and source_operation provider fragments remain object-validated source evidence without flattening dialect facts or extensions; only an explicit canonical_evidence lock may reconstruct that closed provider contract for descriptor mapping after exact inventory reconciliation. When operation accounting cannot obtain required retained-source input, it keeps each locked identity as a non-executable source-retention gap. Source-lock v4 materialization consumes cited descriptors and fails closed when the current runtime cannot faithfully represent a retained contract.

recursive and sibling references retained without unsafe expansion
request- versus response-phase unresolved reference evidence
request body media types and encodings
response status, media, headers, and schema descriptors
source-lock v4 per-operation materialization accounting with typed bindings, citations, raw response-status spellings, and exact runtime-status projections
closed event-schema and declared-batch selector inventories resolved against retained provider bytes
guarantees: bounded fetch and parse budgets
canonical source identity and digest verification
citation retention
ordinary legacy source-contract and operation fragments retain provider bytes after object validation without becoming executable input

an explicit canonical_evidence legacy lock reconstructs only a closed descriptor mapping after exact inventory reconciliation; it does not admit a runtime lane or weaken retained-artifact hash verification for ordinary locks

materialized source-lock rows fail closed when retained runtime reachability, routing, input wire semantics, media, scope, pagination, byte constraints, or exact response-status execution cannot be represented
malformed, unavailable, or unresolved contracts remain explicit gaps

selection.notes: The source lock selects retained artifacts and forms; import produces authoring descriptors and never registers a runtime executor.

constraints: Only contracts stated by retained provider evidence may be imported.

A batch inventory may name only one locked provider operation, canonical schema selectors, a provider-proven maximum, and closed provider envelope/method/response fields; it cannot carry raw executable HTTP.
Reference cycles and unsupported dialect details must remain explicit rather than being guessed or flattened.

Ordinary legacy source_contract and source_operation fragments are source-evidence only; they may retain provider-standard and provider-extension members but cannot supply runtime routing, request, response, credential, or approval behavior. A lock with explicit canonical_evidence may use its closed provider fragments only for deterministic descriptor mapping after inventory reconciliation; it still cannot admit runtime routing, request, response, credential, or approval behavior.
Retained bytes, URLs, and hashes prove provenance, not runtime behavior.

A v4 materialized row must preserve every retained runtime-relevant contract exactly or be represented as cited blocked/unsupported accounting; the materializer does not synthesize a transport escape.

Raw provider response-status spellings remain cited evidence. Unambiguous numeric HTTP values from 100 through 599 are validated without rewriting their source facts; only values that normalize to exact 2xx runtime statuses are materialized. A status range/class or an exact non-2xx contract remains cited blocked with its named runtime gap.
non_goals: Admitting a command, stream, write, or sync mode into runtime.
Inventing provider identifiers, cursors, idempotency, ordering, or media semantics.
Replacing projected connector JSON or certification evidence.

foundations.summary: Projects canonical source operations into connector definitions and global operation ledgers, derives command bindings and flags, and accounts every source operation through declaration admission without treating projection as execution proof. Enabled-connector contracts add a source-lock denominator with exact lane selectors, retained supplemental evidence, and derived complete/partial/not-applicable coverage so an implemented subset is never presented as provider-surface parity. Unmapped mapping is a distinct visible coverage bucket, not a deferred runtime foundation, and may leave a runtime lane implemented with PARTIAL source coverage. A schema-v3 primary contract binds any exact retained provider document in its closed source lock, not a single-document assumption. The existing closed-name admission seam retains source parameter spelling in the descriptor and blocks an unsafe provider spelling rather than creating an ad-hoc alias or raw transport escape. A source-open JSON body may project a documented named field only as a closed root with that field's bounded source shape; a runtime compiler mismatch remains a cited partial command outcome, never a raw-body fallback.

selection.notes: Source identities and declaration bindings select projections; a selected surface sync preserves every unselected runtime endpoint-ledger row. Generated availability remains subject to real runtime preflight.

constraints: Projection must not invent a stream, write action, request field, response policy, or lane absent from the source-backed contract.

A generated direct-read parameter name must satisfy the existing closed engine identifier rule. The source descriptor retains an unsafe provider spelling and the operation remains a cited typed blocked disposition until a separately approved reversible provider-parameter alias foundation exists; projection must not silently omit it.
OpenAPI request projection excludes readOnly properties recursively, including resolved allOf arms, and removes excluded names from required.
Array query encoding must retain the source-declared style, explode behavior, and delimiter; generic value stringification is not source projection.
A required requestBody with one data envelope makes that record field required; an optional requestBody remains optional.

A declared batch is projectable only when a closed v3 batch_action_inventory resolves against retained provider bytes and the definition keeps a typed action allow-list; optional outer query fields remain source-projected while caller-authored subrequest HTTP stays forbidden.

An enabled-contract lane derives complete, partial, or not-applicable coverage from its source denominator. unmapped_mapping is a distinct source-preserving mapping deficit and may make an implemented lane PARTIAL; actual runtime gaps remain named deferred or provider-evidenced outcomes, and neither form can be reported as full provider-surface parity.

A schema-v3 enabled-contract primary source lock may retain several documents. Its evidence digest and byte count must bind one exact retained provider document; validation must not require a single-document lock.

A provider-documented deprecated or destructive operation remains in the source denominator. Its API-surface row must retain source evidence and a named request, approval, response, or other actual foundation gap rather than classifying deprecation or destructive nature as an exclusion.
Aliases and multiple lane bindings must not inflate the provider-operation count.
A projected implemented label is incomplete until the selected runtime path passes preflight.

A selected runtime endpoint-ledger refresh may replace only its named connector entry and must preserve every unselected entry; it must not make an unrelated missing source descriptor an admission gate.

The mapping-only lock view still fails closed on connector ownership, stable identity, citation, location, method, route, counts, source-reference method/identity/location/source-form and legacy supplement binding/count, unavailable reason/source URL, v3 envelope coherence, and the exact source_contract_unavailable disposition.
Schema-version and document-kind selection is presence-aware and closed: foreign, empty, or null variant fields cannot select another wire shape through Go zero values.

A v3 event_schema_inventory is a closed source-selector envelope. Mapping projection ignores it only after rejecting unknown inventory or selector members; source-import alone resolves its canonical selectors against retained provider bytes.

A v3 batch_action_inventory is likewise a closed source-selector envelope. Mapping admission rejects unknown members, source-import resolves its operation/schema/tag facts, and projection preserves only a matching declared_batch definition.
Strict retained-byte and digest validation remains owned by source-import rather than declaration projection.
P5 source-open JSON projection may expose only documented named fields through a closed root; it must not admit arbitrary properties, a generic raw JSON flag, or a connector-specific escape.

If engine.CompileSchema rejects a closed named P5 field, the source row and provider pattern remain retained and every endpoint-bound write command becomes a source-cited partial outcome until an approved execution foundation exists.
non_goals: Executing provider requests or saved syncs.
Supplying missing provider evidence through an admission artifact.
Publishing live certification.

foundations.summary: Runs static and replay-backed bundle conformance, staged live certification, durable cleanup and observation accounting, and source-derived certification matrix generation without configuring or admitting runtime behavior.

source_forms: certification definitions and accepted evidence artifacts
projected connector bundles and source identities
request_response_shapes: direct read and write request-shape assertions
fixture pagination, cursor, schema, delete, and multipart checks
live mutation, read-back, cleanup, and leak observations
per-connector capability and flow matrix cells
sync_modes: declared source and destination modes with exact pair evidence
guarantees: accepted evidence is bound to exact connector, subject, scope, and proof
fixture success remains distinct from live certification
secrets are redacted from reports and persisted evidence
uncertified and not-applicable states remain explicit

selection.notes: Certification observes the already-selected runtime and source-bound definitions; evidence publication cannot create a capability or executor.

constraints: Certification must bind exact source, projected definition, executor, scope, mode, and resource evidence.
A fixture, file name, declaration, or repeated self-claim is not accepted live proof.
Provider refusal and unavailable live environments remain explicit results rather than passing states.
Certification overlays and live credentials validate proof only; their absence or malformed representation cannot admit, suppress, or remap a source operation.
non_goals: Configuring runtime execution or filling missing provider facts.
Promoting a declaration merely because a fixture or certification file exists.
Replacing runtime preflight.
